title: Leningrad: sables, white nights and Russian choirs
summary: Wooding buys sables and a diamond ring in Leningrad, notes the white nights, and praises the Easter choirs as emotional like spirituals.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Friedrichsberg, I think, and waited for Flemming because our trombone player got pneumonia there, see? And, but up in Leningrad we had a wonderful time. We bought some sable coats. I bought a sable coat, and two or three other boys bought sables. And I bought a four carat diamond ring, and things like that. The government hadn't seized yet, you know?
These people had these things and sold them cheap too.
I bought a four-carat diamond ring for $1,000., something like that. Which you can't get one carat for today, you know?
You see, and then I bought my blanket of sables for my wife. She was in Berlin, (unintelligible), because we thought that it wasn't going to be good.
didn't bring her to Russia because I was afraid for her,

But, on the whole, we had a wonderful time. And that was when we went to the Winter Palace in Leningrad. It was Leningrad, then, it was old St. Petersburg. And one thing, I was glad -- a lot of the boys had got in all kinds of fights up there with their family. Those that took their wives. You see, because, at 11 o'clock at night in Petersburg or Leningrad, it's daylight. You can read the newspaper. In the summertime, because that was around the summertime when we got there. And so, we used to, at 11 'o'clock, at 11:30, we were throwing rocks at bullfrogs out there. We left the theater, and we'd go out there. Well, the wives at home say, "Where you been all night?"

"Here it's daybreak and you're just coming home." Well it was only eleven o'clock. They thought we were around having a wonderful time. We did have a wonderful time. The Russian people are like the black people. They have a lot of emotion. They are a really emotional people. And the greatest song that I ever heard -- the greatest singing that I ever heard, outside of black people was the Russian choir on Easter. The Bolsheviks or the Soviets, as now, had cut that out. But nobody had stopped the churches. And we went -- we heard the churches -- there's forty times forty churches in Moscow. And we heard, on Easter, these Russian choirs were something out of this world. Singing. Deep voice and very emotional. Because they're half Asiatic, you know. The Mongols -- when Genghis Khan and his crowd took over, and there's many of them in there. And they were really emotional. And another thing we saw there that I have never seen since, those people in Moscow leaving for Siberia. They walked to Siberia, you know. The captives and all like that. And you could see them. And another thing, those people singing on the Volga. The singing of the Volga -- they have deep voices and emotional voices. I think, it made me think of the Negro spiritual, the Russian folk song.
